title: Volume 1 Chapter 4: Because We're Going to Support You for Life! 1
content: Several days had passed since the photoshoot, bringing us to the end of April. By the time most students had become fairly accustomed to their new classes, the large holiday period spanning late April to early May—the so-called Golden Week—was fast approaching, and many students were already buzzing with excitement. Of course, many were simply looking forward to the break itself, but most were eagerly anticipating a certain event. What event, you ask? If you posed this question to many students, their answer would likely be the same: a mini live concert by the Damenzu.

Dimension Stars!’ first album was set to be released, and to celebrate, a release event was scheduled at the plaza of a shopping mall near the high school. Naturally, news of this had reached the ears of Narukami High School students, and many were determined to attend no matter what. Especially in Class 2-D, where the Damenzu’s double centers, Takanashi Setsuna and Tsukishiro Arisa, were enrolled, nearly the entire class had declared their intention to support them on site.

Correspondingly, the group chat was lively; every night, messages flew back and forth, revealing the class’s high morale. Recently, the excitement had reached a fever pitch, with passionate anonymous letters pouring in day and night, each fan competing to prove they were the biggest supporter. But why was this happening? The answer—and the cause—lay before one girl.
Spreading out cosplay photos of Setsuna and Arisa on the desk, Reika Ijuuin sat with her head in her hands, clearly distressed.
“How did it come to this...?” she muttered, her voice heavy with genuine lament.

She was in her room at the Ijuuin residence in Tokyo. Normally, her maid and attendant, Himeno Ichinose, would be there to care for her and keep her company, but recently, at Reika’s request due to some troubling concerns, she had been isolating herself in her room immediately after returning home. So now, she was alone.

The spacious room, easily over twenty tatami mats in size, was adorned with a lavish chandelier and antique furniture and decorations crafted by renowned artisans—a room befitting a wealthy magnate’s home, dazzlingly splendid.

Normally, this would be a place to relax elegantly with classical music playing softly and a teacup in hand. But now, idol songs blared at full volume, and mugs printed with images of her beloved idols lined the table—a glaring mismatch.
Moreover, the walls were plastered with Dimension Stars! posters, covering every inch and completely shattering any sense of harmony. Yet the room’s owner seemed utterly unconcerned.
Her gaze was fixed on the cosplay photos of her beloved idols, and more importantly, a grave situation was unfolding right before her eyes—there was no room for distraction.
“My Dimension Stars!... My goddesses of fate... to think they allowed that man to take such... outrageous photos...!” she exclaimed.

The photos showed the two beautiful girls dressed in various cosplay outfits—maid uniforms, waitress costumes, cheongsams, cheerleader outfits, mini skirt Santas, leotards, and miko (shrine maiden) attire. They wore a range of expressions, all based on scenarios requested by their classmates.

At first, upon receiving the photos, Reika had been so overjoyed that she forgot her anger toward the detestable Kazuma Kuzuhara and, like her classmates, had written countless anonymous letters. But as time passed and she calmed down, she noticed something unsettling in the idols’ expressions.
Yes, she realized it.
The emotions directed at the photographer in these photos were completely different from those in the posters plastered on the walls.
This was a subtle discrepancy only someone like her—who collected every piece of Damenzu merchandise—could detect.
But realizing this didn’t bring her any luck. Sometimes, ignorance is bliss.
“These are all wonderful photos, but knowing these expressions were created by and directed toward Kazuma Kuzuhara is enough to make my brain explode...” she lamented.
That alone was a headache, but Reika had other worries.
“And that man—he even managed to ensnare Himeno!” she added.
When Himeno returned from the photoshoot that day, her behavior was clearly off. She seemed dazed, as if feverish, and was inattentive even when spoken to.
No matter how much Reika pressed her, Himeno’s answers were vague until finally she said, “I met my fated master.”
At first, Reika thought it was a joke, but seeing the usually expressionless maid blush deeply, she immediately realized Himeno was serious.

“What kind of trick did that man use to capture her...! Why did it have to come to this...?” Reika’s shock at learning that even her childhood friend and trusted maid had been taken by that scumbag was indescribable.
“I only wanted to be near those ladies...” she whispered.

She had sent Himeno as a watcher out of fear that Kazuma might make a move on the Damenzu girls, but that had been a failure. She regretted not going herself. It was too late now; the damage was done.
Even if it was because she feared losing control after seeing her beloved goddesses in cosplay up close, the fact remained that an irreparable situation had unfolded.
Reika clenched her teeth and spat out the name of her hated enemy.
“Unforgivable, Kazuma Kuzuhara...!”

Kazuma Kuzuhara. The worst scumbag who not only targeted the goddesses but even her closest friend. Despite holding the prestigious title of fan club number 001, he was the lowest of the low, trying to exploit and defile his beloved idols.
There was no excuse for Kazuma, but the fact that she once respected number 001 made discovering his true nature all the more infuriating.
“Even if heaven forgives him, I will never forgive that scumbag!” she vowed.
But then, what should she do?
“Ask Kurosu to get rid of that man... no, that won’t do. Kazuma Kuzuhara would surely run crying to Setsuna and Arisa. If that happens, my standing with them will only worsen...” she reasoned.
That wouldn’t do. Even now, her words failed to reach the girls.
Since Kazuma’s transfer, she had tried to explain how terrible he was whenever possible, but it had been utterly ineffective.
If anything, she sensed their eyes held a mix of exasperation when looking at her.
(Is it the difference in years spent together? They know he’s my childhood friend, but... ugh, what a troublesome man...)
Frustrated, she ground her teeth.
As a wealthy heiress trained in the ways of leadership, she understood how important trust was, but she had never faced someone who had already earned it.
She had to admit her lack of experience as a high schooler, but she had no idea how to separate those two from that man.
That was the root of her deep worry.
(If I ask Himeno for advice, it’ll probably be useless too.)
Her usual go-to, Himeno, was already ensnared by Kazuma.
Even if she consulted her about him, it would likely be pointless—or worse, she might leak information behind her back.
Though she wanted to deny such thoughts, the possibility kept her from acting.
“Ah, what should I do!?” she cried out.
This wasn’t how it was supposed to be. Meeting Dimension Stars! was supposed to be her destiny.
Her emotions had surged so strongly that she transferred schools just to be near them.
She had no regrets about that, but Kazuma’s presence was the one and only miscalculation.
She had believed the future ahead would be the best possible, so the shock was indescribably painful.
Feeling her carefully imagined future crumble, Reika reached a conclusion.
That man, Kazuma Kuzuhara, must be eliminated at all costs.
Kazuma Kuzuhara was a cancerous tumor threatening to destroy both her and Dimension Stars!’ futures.
That scumbag was no one who should be near the goddesses.
With renewed resolve, she asked herself what to do.
“If only there were a good solution... ugh, if I could solve this with money, that would be the quickest way...!”
She stopped herself mid-sentence, suddenly struck by an idea.
—“Support me for life, and keep me comfortable, okay? If I ever have to work, even though we’re childhood friends, I won’t forgive you.”
Kazuma had said something like this to Setsuna on his first day at the new school. Looking back, it was an utterly scumbag remark, but he had told Arisa the same thing.
“So, ‘support’ means that man needs money, right?”
Then maybe there was a quick fix.
“If I give him enough money as a breakup settlement... maybe I could save Setsuna-sama and Arisa-sama...?”
It was possible. Money was a common adult solution, and the Ijuuin family had used such methods many times before to quietly settle matters.
Though young, Reika had despised such dirty tactics and never thought she’d have to use them. But if that was what it took to pry those two from that man, the price was worth it.
Her pride and Dimension Stars!’ future—she weighed both on the scales but hesitated not a moment.
“Desperate times call for desperate measures.”
Yes. A monetary solution.
An impossible method for an ordinary high schooler, who could only move limited sums. Normally, it would be ruled out immediately.
But she, Reika Ijuuin, could choose this path.
Born and raised a wealthy heiress, with ample funds at her disposal, no one else could do it.
So she had no choice but to act. She could save them.
“Wait and see, Kazuma Kuzuhara. I, Reika Ijuuin, will protect Dimension Stars! no matter what...!”
Even if it meant bending her beliefs and sullying her hands, she vowed to protect her precious treasures.
Rising with determination, she clapped her hands, and immediately there was a knock at the door.
“Milady, you called?”
“Yes, Kurosu. I have something I want prepared. Cash... let’s say, one hundred million yen. Prepare it for me.”
She hadn’t given much thought to the exact amount. She simply guessed that such a large sum would easily lure that lowlife.
“One hundred million, you say?”
“Don’t ask why. It’s urgent. Have it ready by tomorrow morning. And keep it secret from Himeno, understood?”
“Yes, milady,” the black-suited man bowed and left the room.
As the door closed, Reika sat back down. Now all that remained was to wait for tomorrow.
Thinking it over again, one hundred million yen was an extraordinary sum for a high schooler.
Most people would be dazzled by such an amount and accept it without hesitation.
Especially a vulgar man like that scumbag. If it could protect Dimension Stars!, one hundred million was nothing.
“Phew...” she sighed, glancing at the photos on the desk.
Overcome by their preciousness, she smiled, and it felt as if they smiled back at her.
“I will definitely save you...”
All for the sake of her goddesses of fate.
With strong resolve, the night deepened.
The day before the start of the long holiday, I left home as usual and walked the familiar path to school.
But there was one difference: my heart was as clear as the cloudless blue sky above.
The reason was obvious: Golden Week was about to begin.
Recently, I’d had less time to watch streams or play games, so during the break, I planned to do whatever I wanted.
Playing games all night was an option, as was ordering delicious food without restraint.
Only one thing was disappointing: my gaming buddy Harukaze said she’d be busy during Golden Week and probably wouldn’t have much time to quest with me.
Well, she had her reasons, so I couldn’t complain. Anyway, I was determined to play hard this Golden Week.
Arisa, who usually nagged me about my behavior, had been especially busy these past few days preparing and rehearsing for the mini live in town, so she and Setsuna would be late to school today.
Once the holidays started, they’d be even busier with lessons and such, dedicating themselves fully.
Knowing no one would complain about me playing around all day was a huge plus.
I’d even gotten a maid who said she’d support me financially, so my extra income would probably increase.
Anyway, I was feeling great in both body and mind.
“Hmm-huh-huh-hun. What should I do tomorrow~♪”
Humming a cheerful tune, I quickly reached the classroom.
Time flies when you’re in a good mood, they say.
Still in high spirits, I threw open the classroom door.
“Morning, everyone!”
The moment I greeted them, I felt all eyes turn toward me.
Among those staring was Nekomiya, who glared at me briefly before looking away and returning to chatting with nearby girls.
That was unusual for her—apparently, she hated me after the last incident.
(Hmm, that’s a problem. Well, can’t be helped.)
I smiled wryly at the harsh reaction from a classmate I’d known since middle school.
Several others noticed me and raised their hands in greeting.
“Hey, Kazuma! Good morning!”
“Yo, Kazuma!”
“Man, Kuzuhara’s looking sharp today! As always, you’re the coolest! Hey, ladies’ man!”
These friendly greetings came from the same group I’d given the cosplay photos to.
Among them were Sayama and Gotou-kun, who shamelessly tried to curry favor with me, but I didn’t mind.
“Haha, don’t flatter me so much, you’re making me blush.”
“No, seriously, we mean it! Right, guys?”
The boys nodded. Since then, we’d managed to build a better relationship.
Apparently, they were pleased with the photos and had also been fending off other Damenzu fans from different classes demanding copies.
Having a rare item only they possessed softened their attitude toward me.
(What fickle guys. But that’s idol otaku for you.)
I couldn’t say I didn’t notice their sudden change of heart, but that was exactly what I wanted.
People feel superior when they have something others want. Otaku are especially weak to the word “limited.”
Sure, I could have sold the photos for money, but what I wanted was peace in the class—not something money could buy.
It would be foolish to lose trust and worsen my reputation for a quick buck.
Sometimes you have to lose to win. Even if it doesn’t make money, having a premium item exclusive to us strengthened our bond and made them accept me.
“Hey, master. You’re late.”
Lost in thought, I headed to my seat, only to find someone already there.
Seeing who it was, I couldn’t help but frown.
“What are you doing here? Your class is upstairs.”
“Don’t be so stiff. Aren’t we friends?”
Hijiri, the flashy senior, stood up and forcibly draped his arm around my shoulder.
His familiar, casual attitude was unchanged since we first met, but now he treated me differently.
He’d started calling me “master” and showing admiration.
He said my words had opened his eyes—that he wanted to live an easy life with women spoiling him, so he wanted to learn from me how to seduce idols and get them to spoil him.
At first, I was taken aback and refused, but he occasionally showed up to bother me, so I’d half given up and just dealt with it.
He hadn’t harmed me, and I’d gotten him to promise to curb his womanizing until he learned my methods.
Besides, I was honestly curious about what he knew that I didn’t.
If he wanted to learn how to get women to spoil him, I could learn the secrets of being a playboy from him.
Our interests aligned in a way.
“Hey, got any free time during Golden Week? If so, let’s hang out. I know a good spot, and maybe we can try to pick up some rich girls.”
“Sure, but you pay and take responsibility, okay? I don’t want to get stuck with some landmine.”
“You’re even worse than me, huh...”
“It’s only right the inviter takes responsibility. I’m just stating the obvious.”
As I half-heartedly humored Hijiri, more classmates trickled into the classroom.
Some greeted cheerfully; others yawned lazily.
But all looked bright, clearly excited for the upcoming break.
We’d get through today for that reason. Though unspoken, a shared atmosphere was building in the class.
I felt the same. I didn’t want any trouble before the holidays.
Better to have a smooth day.
I was eagerly awaiting homeroom time.
Just as I was about to suggest to Hijiri, who was still outside the class despite being a senior, that we head back, someone appeared.
“Good morning.”
The familiar, painfully bright golden blonde stepped into the classroom.
The golden and glamorous girl was none other than Ijuuin.
Come to think of it, I hadn’t seen her today yet.
Even someone so conspicuous, I hadn’t noticed her absence—habituation was scary.
Though only about two weeks had passed since her transfer, I was getting used to her presence.
Hijiri next to me, however, was different. Nudging my arm, he whispered.
“Hey, that flashy girl who looks rich—is she the rumored transfer student, Ijuuin?”
“Yeah. She’s the heiress of the Ijuuin conglomerate.”
“The Ijuuin conglomerate!? That mega-rich family!? If I hooked up with her, I’d be set for life...!”
Hijiri swallowed hard, probably imagining a future where he’d captured Ijuuin.
But that was reckless.
“Better not. Going after Ijuuin is way too risky. She’s got powerful backing. If you mess with her and end up buried in concrete in Tokyo Bay, that’d be stupid. It’s smarter to aim lower.”
“Hm... true. She’s a great catch, but if you say so, master, I’ll pass.”
Hijiri backed off easily after my whisper.
Relieved, I continued.
“Good call. Oh, and don’t even think about touching the girl behind Ijuuin.”
“Huh? Why not? Wait, you don’t mean...”
“Yeah. That maid is mine. She’s agreed to support me financially, so I’d be in trouble if anyone messed with her.”
“No way! Master, you’re amazing...!”
Hijiri looked at me with sparkling admiration, unlike his usual flashy self.
After all the times I’d been called scum, it felt nice to be seen with pure eyes.
Feeling elated, I tried to respond with a cynical smile, but—
“Hmph, not so much...”
“Hey, what are you two talking about?”
Suddenly cutting in was Ijuuin, who had somehow moved in front of my seat.
“I’m just sharing some info between guys,” I said.
